title: Digital Product and Service Management: Key Concepts

header.html: Define digital product and service management, product, service, digital product, digital service, good, continual improvement, the lifecycle, utility, warranty, user experience and sustainability; explain service offerings, service interactions, service actions, transfer of goods and access to resources; know the benefits of ITIL
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), categories 1.1 and 1.3

html:
1The big idea

ITIL is a framework of best practice for digital product and service management: how an organization creates, delivers and continually improves products and services so that value is co-created with the people who use them.

Old wording ITIL 4 spoke of IT service management and only services. Version 5 treats products and services as two sides of the same digital solution.

2Product, service and good

Term Meaning in plain words
Digital product and service management Managing digital products and services across their whole life so they create value
Product A configuration of resources (people, processes, technology, information) designed to offer value to a consumer
Service A means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating the outcomes consumers want, without the consumer managing the specific costs and risks
Digital product A product that depends on digital technology
Digital service A service that is enabled by digital technology
Good An item whose ownership is transferred to the consumer
Exam tip

. Product = the configuration of resources. Service = the way value is co-created, with the provider carrying the costs and risks. A product can be offered as a service. [Verify live]

Continual improvement is the recurring activity of improving products, services, practices and the whole ITIL Value System. The ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle is the model of eight activities (discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support) that apply to every product and service (Modules 5 to 7).

3Service offerings

Term Meaning
Service offering A formal description of one or more services designed to meet the needs of a target consumer group
Service interactions The exchanges between the provider and the consumer while the service is used
Service actions Actions the provider performs for the consumer, such as running a process
Transfer of goods Ownership of a good passes to the consumer
Access to resources The consumer may use a resource (a licence, a subscription) but the provider keeps ownership

An offering can combine goods, access to resources and service actions. Example: a laptop bought outright is a transfer of goods; a cloud tool used by subscription is access to resources; the help desk fixing a fault is a service action.

Exam tip

. Owns it afterward = transfer of goods. Uses it but does not own it = access to resources. Someone does work for you = service action.

4Utility, warranty, user experience, sustainability

Term Question it answers
Utility Is it fit for purpose? (does what is needed)
Warranty Is it fit for use? (available, secure, reliable, enough capacity)
User experience How does using it feel to the people involved?
Sustainability Can it continue without harming people, the environment or the organization over time?

These four, with outcomes, costs and risks, are the areas of value (Module 2). [Verify live]

5Benefits of ITIL

Who Benefit (in short)
Enterprises A common language, better value from digital investment, better alignment with business goals
Managed service providers Clearer service offerings, better relationships, repeatable good practice
Digital product vendors Guidance to build, run and support products so customers get value
Digital product and service management professionals Recognized skills, a shared vocabulary, a path to higher ITIL qualifications
Exam tip

. In a List question, check each statement on its own: "fit for purpose" is utility, "fit for use" is warranty. Swapping them is the classic trap.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Contoso Retail buys a point-of-sale tablet and now owns it. Which concept does this describe?

  • AAccess to resources
  • BTransfer of goods
  • CA service action
  • DA service interaction
Show the answer

Answer: B. Ownership passes to the consumer, so it is a transfer of goods.

S2A company pays a monthly fee to use a cloud file-sharing tool that the vendor keeps owning and running. Which concept applies?

  • ATransfer of goods only
  • BA product specification
  • CAccess to resources
  • DA known error
Show the answer

Answer: C. The consumer may use the resource while the provider keeps ownership.

S3Which statement about utility and warranty is CORRECT? (1) Utility means the product is fit for purpose. (2) Utility means the product is fit for use. (3) Warranty means the product is fit for use. (4) Warranty means the product is fit for purpose.

  • A1 and 2
  • B1 and 3
  • C3 and 4
  • D2 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: B. Utility is fit for purpose and warranty is fit for use.

S4Identify the missing word(s). A [ ? ] is a formal description of one or more services designed to address the needs of a target consumer group.

  • AService request
  • BService level
  • CService offering
  • DService journey
Show the answer

Answer: C. That is the definition of a service offering.

S5The help desk resets a user's locked account. Which concept is this?

  • AA good
  • BA transfer of goods
  • CSustainability
  • DA service action
Show the answer

Answer: D. The provider performs an action for the consumer.

S6What describes a service, as ITIL defines it?

  • AA set of hardware items the customer keeps
  • BA written contract between two suppliers
  • CA means of enabling value co-creation while the provider carries specific costs and risks
  • DA list of known errors with workarounds
Show the answer

Answer: C. A service enables co-created value without the consumer managing those costs and risks.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Define a product.

Show the answer

A configuration of an organization's resources designed to offer value to a consumer.

R2What question does utility answer?

Show the answer

Is it fit for purpose?

R3What question does warranty answer?

Show the answer

Is it fit for use?

R4What is a good?

Show the answer

An item whose ownership is transferred to the consumer.

R5Name the three things a service offering can combine.

Show the answer

Goods, access to resources and service actions.

R6What are the eight lifecycle activities?

Show the answer

Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver and support.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Product / service resources configured to offer value / enabling co-creation, provider carries costs and risks
Good ownership is transferred
Offering goods + access to resources + service actions
Utility / warranty fit for purpose / fit for use
Also user experience and sustainability are areas of value
